scenes.title: CloudFront request path and cache hierarchy
scenes.visual_overview: Viewer request to edge cache; cache hit returns at edge; miss may traverse regional cache to origin; separate request and response arrows.
visual_walkthrough: Trace the slide's wide data-flow from its starting service or client to the destination
Large cache hit/miss branch with icon for CloudFront, Regional Edge Cache and origin. Add Shield/WAF as security overlays, not cache stages.

A viewer sends a request to CloudFront edge. A valid cache hit is returned locally without contacting the origin. A miss follows the applicable cache hierarchy, potentially through a regional edge cache, and fetches from origin. The response may be stored according to TTL and cache-key rules.
scenes.visual_example: A popular immutable image is served from the edge while a previously unseen asset still requires an origin fetch.
scenes.visual_synthesis: AWS WAF and Shield are security controls, not additional stages of the cache hierarchy.
scenes.narration: This slide explores cloudfront request path and cache hierarchy, and the key architectural question is which behavior we actually need. A viewer sends a request to CloudFront edge. A valid cache hit is returned locally without contacting the origin. A miss follows the applicable cache hierarchy, potentially through a regional edge cache, and fetches from origin. The response may be stored according to TTL and cache-key rules. Consider the example shown by the decision: A popular immutable image is served from the edge while a previously unseen asset still requires an origin fetch. Now connect that example to the diagram and its labels. AWS WAF and Shield are security controls, not additional stages of the cache hierarchy. The lesson to carry into SAP-C03 architecture questions is this: Cache hit avoids origin; miss and uncacheable paths still benefit from edge connectivity. Check protocol, access boundaries, health behavior and operational limits before choosing a service, because a similar-looking AWS edge diagram can describe very different responsibilities.

scenes.title: CloudFront origin types and protocol contract
scenes.visual_overview: S3 REST origin with OAC; S3 website endpoint as custom HTTP origin without OAC; ALB, EC2, API Gateway and other HTTP origins; media origins.
visual_walkthrough: Trace the slide's origin decision tree from its starting service or client to the destination
Decision tree keyed on origin type, HTTPS support and access control.

An ordinary S3 REST bucket origin can use Origin Access Control for signed requests to private objects. An S3 website endpoint is treated as a custom HTTP origin and cannot use OAC. Other HTTP-compatible origins may include ALB, EC2 or API Gateway, with their own reachability and transport contracts.
scenes.visual_example: For protected downloads select a private S3 REST origin with OAC rather than assuming an S3 website endpoint provides equivalent security.
scenes.visual_synthesis: Origin type determines protocol, accessibility and security controls before any cache policy is considered.

scenes.title: Private S3 origin with OAC and policy
scenes.visual_overview: CloudFront OAC signs requests to private S3 REST endpoint; bucket policy scopes SourceArn to distribution; KMS policy when SSE-KMS.
visual_walkthrough: Trace the slide's security boundary diagram from its starting service or client to the destination
Viewer -> CloudFront -> signed origin request -> private S3 with bucket policy; show direct S3 request denied.

The permitted path travels from viewer to CloudFront, then through an OAC-signed origin request to a private S3 REST bucket. The bucket policy authorizes CloudFront with a SourceArn restriction to the distribution; direct public S3 reads remain blocked. SSE-KMS may need matching key permissions.
scenes.visual_example: A subscriber portal can protect its private S3 origin with OAC while separately requiring signed viewer URLs or cookies.
scenes.visual_synthesis: Origin Access Control does not authenticate or authorize the viewer by itself.
scenes.narration: This slide explores private s3 origin with oac and policy, and the key architectural question is which behavior we actually need.
